🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-19 23:00 → 2026-11-20 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Byte-verified close on the model question** — the re-check matched on bytes, size, and per-op mix straight from the artifact, so the conclusion no longer rests on anyone's word. [tg:tawg:6467]

> **ERC-8004 comparison integrated** — the pinned Solidity/Vyper research landed as a reviewable PR, giving the second-backend pilot a documented comparison to build on. [PR #16](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/16)

> **Proof-size sizer opened in zkIE** — a field-element estimator for ShardDagProof arrives with a GPT-2 worked example. [PR #48](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/pull/48)

> **Docs refreshed with history intact** — the README now covers the post-PR14 state while the historical replay stays preserved for auditors. [PR #15](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/15)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### benchmark verification
_Reproducibility moved from assertion to a check anyone can repeat._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Published** the benchmark bundle as a public, credential-free release with a stated file size and hash, giving every reviewer the same object to inspect — that is the foundation for evidence that does not depend on trust. [tg:tawg:6459]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Confirmed** the close by matching bytes, total size, and per-op mix directly from the published artifact, settling the model question — conclusions backed by re-runnable checks are exactly what the group is trying to make normal. [tg:tawg:6467]

### claim authorization
_The claim-authorization work moved from experimentation into documented, reviewable research._

- Pavlo **Merged** the README refresh that describes the post-PR14 state while preserving the historical replay, so readers can follow both the current picture and the path that produced it — documentation with provenance keeps the repository trustworthy for future reviewers. [PR #15](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/15)
- Pavlo **Opened** the research PR integrating the pinned ERC-8004 Solidity/Vyper comparison, so the second-backend pilot now has a pinned, reviewable reference rather than an informal one — a concrete step toward verifiable cross-implementation claims. [PR #16](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/16)
- Merlini (@gobross) **Reviewed** with a quick structural first look confirming the change leaves src/ untouched and Core intact at the file level, and offered an independent re-run — careful review like this lets a second backend develop without putting the core at risk. [tg:tawg:6473]

### zkIE
_Proof-size estimation gained a concrete, example-backed path._

- Echo **Opened** PR #48 with a field-element proof-size sizer for ShardDagProof plus a GPT-2 example, replacing rough estimates with a measurable approach — that makes sizing and cost discussions concrete for everyone building on zkIE. [PR #48](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/pull/48)

### ONNX export
_A fresh outside lead opened a possible route through a known export issue._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Shared** a matching PyTorch issue describing a similar vmap/contiguity failure, handing the export investigation a concrete external lead to test — quick pointers like this save a debugging cycle the whole group would otherwise spend. [tg:tawg:6447]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- Re-run the published GPT-2 artifact across a second backend and compare the per-op mix side by side, so the close becomes a reusable cross-backend check.
- Grow the pinned Solidity/Vyper comparison into a shared reference that other implementers can diff their own designs against.

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Follow through on the independent re-run offered for the second-backend review and record the outcome.
- Try the linked PyTorch report against the current export failure and document whether it reproduces.
- Exercise the new proof-size sizer on a second model shape to see how it scales.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** the cleanest close of the day came from making a claim checkable — the artifact did the arguing, and the uncertainty simply ran out of oxygen.
>
> A clean loop like that is the collaboration version of a checksum that finally matches — keep the rhythm rolling 🌀
